hindi: कुरु वंश के सबसे बड़े, प्रतापी पितामह भीष्म ने दुर्योधन के मन में हर्ष उत्पन्न करते हुए सिंह की दहाड़ जैसी ऊँची आवाज़ की और अपना शंख बजाया।
english: To fill Duryodhana with cheer, Bhishma, the mighty grandsire and eldest of the Kurus, roared loudly like a lion and blew his conch shell.
deeper: Duryodhana had just spoken with worry hidden inside his words. He kept counting armies and asking everyone to protect Bhishma. Bhishma, the oldest and most respected person on the field, seems to hear that worry. He answers without words, with a lion’s roar and the sound of his conch.

A conch in ancient India was like a bugle. It told everyone that the time had come. Bhishma’s blast was a loud signal that the battle was beginning. It was also a gift of courage to the people standing around him. Sometimes a big, confident sound can lift a heavy heart.

But look closely. Bhishma lifted Duryodhana’s spirits, yet the joy was only on the surface. The Gita will soon show that real peace does not come from loud noise. It comes from knowing what is right. A cheerful roar can raise courage, but only a clear mind shows us where that courage should be used.
words: the eldest of the Kuru family
background: The Kauravas and the Pandavas stood on the field of Kurukshetra, ready to fight. The blind king Dhritarashtra was far away in the palace, and his minister Sanjaya was telling him everything that happened. Duryodhana went to his teacher Drona and named the great warriors on both sides (1.3–1.9).
Duryodhana then compared the two armies (1.10). He ordered his commanders to stand firm and, above all, to protect Bhishma (1.11). Now, in verse 12, Bhishma answers with a roar and a conch blast.
lessons: A kind or brave word from an elder can lift someone’s worried heart.
Bhishma did not hide his strength; he used it to give others confidence.
Listen to the worry behind the words
Duryodhana sounded confident, but his anxious orders showed how he really felt.
Loud is not the same as right
A big sound can cheer us up, but we still must ask whether our cause is good.
People who are respected can make others feel calm or fearful, so they should speak and act wisely.
examples: Aarav’s cricket team was losing and everyone looked sad. Their captain clapped loudly and shouted, “We can still do this!” The team stood straighter and played harder.
Meera was nervous before her dance show. Her dadi hugged her and said, “You will shine, beta.” Meera felt her fear shrink.
Rohan forgot his first line in the school play. His teacher gave him a big thumbs up from the side of the stage. He took a breath and went on.
On Sports Day, Kavya’s whole class shouted her name as she ran. She did not win, but she felt strong because they cheered.
Ishaan kept boasting, “I will top the exam, no problem!” His sister noticed he kept checking his bag again and again. She gently asked if he was nervous, and he nodded.
Tara’s little puppy barked loudly at a strange noise, but hid behind her legs. Tara learned that loud sounds can cover up fear.
During Ganesh Chaturthi, the dhol beats made everyone in Sneha’s lane feel joyful and ready to dance. Music can wake up courage and happiness together.
Before a class debate, Dev felt pumped up by his friends’ cheers. Then he asked himself, “Is my argument true and fair?” Being happy is good, but being right matters too.

story.title: Devavrata Becomes Bhishma
paras: Long ago, Prince Devavrata was the son of King Shantanu of Hastinapur. He was brave, wise and loved by everyone. One day the king fell in love with Satyavati, the daughter of a fisher chief.

Her father said she could marry the king only if her children, and not Devavrata, would one day sit on the throne. Shantanu could not agree. He returned to the palace sad and silent, and Devavrata noticed his father’s sorrow.

Devavrata went to the fisher chief and made a great promise: he would never take the throne, and he would never marry, so that no quarrel could ever arise. The sky seemed to shake with the force of such a vow. People began to call him Bhishma, which means “the one of the terrible vow.”

Bhishma kept his word all his life and served the Kuru family faithfully, as a grandsire to all. That is why, on the field of Kurukshetra, everyone looked up to him, and why his lion’s roar in this verse made his side feel so strong.
story.moral: Lesson: A person who keeps their word and cares for their family earns the kind of respect that gives courage to others.
